page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512F and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage bundled with this server, but it is Premium Storage capable, requiring remote storage attachments. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark evaluations place the D8s_v4 consistently in the average performance tier for most workloads. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 1411.98 and 7435.42 respectively, aligning with the middle 50% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is measured at 414.43 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 44.87 GB/sec for uncached large block reads. In file processing, single-threaded gzip compression achieves 23.82 GB/sec, though bzip3 decompression performance is weak, scoring 8.78 GB/sec single-threaded and 25.34 GB/sec multi-threaded. Database operations via Redis SET reach 6.84 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is recorded at 6.85 GB/sec. Large language model inference using a small 135M model shows a weak prompt processing speed of 380.28 tokens per second, but text generation maintains an average rate of 124.04 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8s_v4 offers a standard resource density suitable for mainstream enterprise workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory or compute-optimized hardware. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, which necessitates reliance on network-attached Premium Storage and may introduce latency for I/O-heavy operations. Additionally, its weak performance in complex decompression and LLM prompt processing suggests it is less optimal for heavy data science or advanced analytical tasks. The server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, standard database operations, software compilation, and basic text or image processing.
